empty_cells: r2 in human plasma or human whole blood at 7 T, any agent: no readable source (the 7 T papers read give r1 only).

r2 in human plasma or human whole blood at 1.5 T and 3 T measured in the source itself: no readable source. The only r2 values at 1.5/3 T in plasma are the secondary Rohrer 2005 values (bovine plasma) in Robic 2019 Table 1; r2 in human whole blood (Shen 2019, Maki 2026) is behind a paywall.

r1 and r2 at 4.7 T in human plasma, human blood or water for the extracellular agents (gadoterate, gadobutrol, gadopentetate, and so on): no readable primary source and no r2. Rohrer 2005 has them but is closed; two of its 4.7 T r1 values (gadopentetate in plasma, gadofosveset in water) are recorded as secondary through Richardson 2012. Other readable 4.7 T values: gadoterate in liver perfusate (r1, r2*), gadoxetate in rat blood (r1), gadofosveset in PBS at 21 °C (r1, r2).
r2 at 9.4 T for the extracellular clinical agents: no readable source (Fries 2019 abstract gives r1 only). Only gadofosveset has r1 and r2 at 9.4 T (PBS, 21 °C).
Any relaxivity above 9.4 T (11.7 T to 18 T) for a clinical gadolinium agent at or near 37 °C: searched (PubMed and Europe PMC, terms 11.7 T, 14.1 T, 16.4 T, 17.6 T), no readable source found.
r2* per agent in human plasma or human whole blood: no readable number. Leads: Blockley 2008, Maki 2026, Heidenreich 2026. Patil 2013 gives only a nonlinear calibration.
r1 in water or saline at 7 T for agents other than gadopiclenol: no readable source.
r1 in human serum/plasma at 1.5 T measured directly (not 1.41 T) for gadopiclenol: no readable source.
